'''Trilochan Pradhan''' (3 January 1929 – 4 December 2021) was an Indian scientist.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Noted physicist Trilochan Pradhan passes away at 93|url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/odisha/2021/Dec/05/noted-physicist-trilochan-pradhan-passes-away-at-93-2392035.html|access-date=2021-12-05|work=[[The New Indian Express]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=4 December 2021|title=Former Utkal University VC Dr. Trilochan Pradhan Passes Away|url=https://pragativadi.com/former-utkal-university-vc-dr-trilochan-pradhan-passes-away/|access-date=4 December 2021|work=[[Pragativadi]]|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Career==
Pradhan obtained his PhD from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1956. He headed the Theoretical Nuclear Physics Division at the Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics from 1964 to 1974, was the founding director of the [[Institute of Physics, Bhubaneswar]] from 1974 to 1989 and served as the vice chancellor of [[Utkal University]] from 1989 to 1991.<ref name="MohantyMohanty2006">{{cite book|author1=Jagannath Mohanty|author2=Sudhansu Mohanty|title=In Quest of Quality Education and Literature: An Autobiography|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EXmnZw99mXgC&pg=PA190|date=1 January 2006|publisher=Deep & Deep Publications|isbn=978-81-7629-764-6|pages=190–}}</ref>

==Books==
* The Photon, (Nova Science Publishers, New York), 2001<ref name="Pradhan2001">{{cite book|author=Trilochan Pradhan|title=The Photon|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=P2UTBEeHL9kC|date=1 January 2001|publisher=Nova Publishers|isbn=978-1-56072-928-0}}</ref>
* Quantum Mechanics (University Press of Hyderabad)<ref name="Pradhan2009">{{cite book|author=Trilochan Pradhan|title=Quantum Mechanics|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2pVAngEACAAJ|year=2009|publisher=Anshan|isbn=978-1-84829-038-9}}</ref>
* Electron Capture by Protons Passing through Hydrogen<ref name="Pradhan1956">{{cite book|author=Trilochan Pradhan|title=Electron Capture by Protons Passing Through Hydrogen|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hDdLOAAACAAJ|year=1956|publisher=University of Chicago, Department of Physics.}}</ref>

* [[Padma Bhusan]], 1990<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://archive.india.gov.in/myindia/padmabhushan_awards_list1.php?start=500 |title=Padma Bhushan Awardees - Padma Awards - My India, My Pride - Know India: National Portal of India |access-date=26 November 2015 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304083908/http://archive.india.gov.in/myindia/padmabhushan_awards_list1.php?start=500 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
